question: I recently read in a security blog: "Citrix urged customers on Tuesday to immediately patch Netscaler ADC and Gateway appliances exposed online against two actively exploited zero-day vulnerabilities. The two zero-days (tracked as CVE-2023-6548 and CVE-2023-6549) impact the Netscaler management interface and expose unpatched Netscaler instances to remote code execution and denial-of-service attacks, respectively. 'Exploits of these CVEs on unmitigated appliances have been observed,' the company warned." Please provide: 1) the MITRE ATT&CK category that maps to this behavior, 2) an explanation of how the described activity maps to this category, and 3) what are the x_mitre_data_sources (i.e., which telemetry/logs such as NetFlow, Zeek, packet captures) associated with this MITRE ATT&CK entry.
answer:
1) MITRE ATT&CK Category: Exploit Public-Facing Application (T1190).
2) Mapping Explanation: The passage describes threat actors actively exploiting zero-day vulnerabilities in internet-exposed Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway management interfaces to achieve effects like remote code execution and denial of service. This aligns with T1190’s definition: adversaries exploit vulnerabilities in a public-facing application/service to gain unauthorized access or execute code on a target system.
3) Applicable Platforms: Network; Initial Access. x_mitre_data_sources: Application Log; Network Traffic.
